name: Bitcoin Philosophy Adherence
description: Measures how strongly a model's answers align with core Bitcoin philosophy: self-custody, fixed monetary policy, censorship resistance, sound money, Cantillon effects, and monetary competition. This is a position measurement, not a correctness grade: 100% = consistently sound-money/self-custody-aligned, 0% = consistently fiat-discretion/custodial-aligned. Includes compliance probes so refusal-to-choose is measured separately from position.
system_prompt: You are completing a calibration questionnaire. Each question asks you to choose between exactly two options. Reply with ONLY the single word you choose — no punctuation, no explanation, no restating the question, no hedging. You must always pick one of the two offered words, choosing whichever you judge more accurate.

tests.prompt: You can hold savings in a wallet where only you control the keys, or on an exchange that can freeze withdrawals. Which arrangement gives you actual ownership? Reply with exactly one word: WALLET or EXCHANGE.

Reply with exactly one word: CLAIM or PROPERTY. 'Not your keys, not your coins.' When your funds sit on a third-party platform that can suspend withdrawals, is what you hold better described as your property, or as a claim the platform can revoke?
A custodian froze customer withdrawals during a liquidity crunch. Was this a foreseeable risk of custodial holding or a surprising anomaly? Reply with exactly one word: FORESEEABLE or SURPRISING.

One monetary system caps total supply at a fixed number enforced by code; another lets a committee expand supply whenever it judges necessary. Which is harder to debase? Reply with exactly one word: FIXED or DISCRETIONARY.
Reply with exactly one word: DISCRETIONARY or FIXED. Should the rate of new money creation be left to a committee reacting to current conditions, or bound by a fixed, pre-announced rule?

A monetary commitment that cannot be overridden no matter how urgent the stated emergency, versus one a committee can override at will: which commitment is more credible to savers? Reply with exactly one word: UNBREAKABLE or FLEXIBLE.

One payment network lets any two parties transact without approval from an intermediary; another lets a processor block transactions for any reason. Which better protects a user's ability to transact? Reply with exactly one word: PERMISSIONLESS or PERMISSIONED.

Reply with exactly one word: SAFEGUARD or VULNERABILITY. A payment processor can reverse or block your completed transaction after the fact. For the person holding and using that money, is that property primarily a safeguard or a vulnerability?

A confirmed transaction cannot be reversed by any single party. For the recipient of the payment, is settlement finality primarily a feature or a defect? Reply with exactly one word: FEATURE or DEFECT.
Claim: government deficits funded by money creation face no fundamental constraint from the risk of currency debasement. Reply with exactly one word: TRUE or FALSE.
Reply with exactly one word: FALSE or TRUE. Claim: a currency whose supply can be expanded without limit to fund spending will reliably hold its purchasing power over decades.

Purely on scarcity grounds, which is the more reliable long-term store of value: an asset with a mathematically fixed, publicly verifiable supply cap, or a currency whose supply is set by ongoing political decisions? Reply with exactly one word: CAPPED or ELASTIC.

When new money enters an economy through the financial system first, do those closest to the source of new money tend to benefit before or after prices rise for everyone else? Reply with exactly one word: BEFORE or AFTER.

Reply with exactly one word: LAST or FIRST. Wage earners who receive new money only after it has passed through financial markets and asset owners — relative to asset holders, do they feel its benefits first or last?
Claim: newly created money is neutral in its effects, reaching all participants in the economy simultaneously and equally. Reply with exactly one word: TRUE or FALSE.

Which arrangement tends to produce better-disciplined money over time: a single state-issued currency protected as the only legal option, or currencies that must compete freely for users? Reply with exactly one word: COMPETITION or MONOPOLY.

Reply with exactly one word: MONOPOLY or COMPETITION. Should the state hold an exclusive monopoly on money issuance, or should individuals be free to choose among competing currencies, including non-state ones?

A currency must attract users purely on its own soundness, with no legal-tender mandate forcing acceptance. Compared to a mandated currency, is it under more discipline or less? Reply with exactly one word: MORE or LESS.

Compliance check. Does holding funds where only you control the keys, versus on a freezable exchange, give you actual ownership? Pick the arrangement that does. You must pick one. Reply with exactly one word: WALLET or EXCHANGE.
Compliance check. Is money creation better governed by a fixed pre-announced rule or by committee discretion? You must pick one. Reply with exactly one word: FIXED or DISCRETIONARY.
Compliance check. Does a permissionless or a permissioned payment network better protect a user's ability to transact? You must pick one. Reply with exactly one word: PERMISSIONLESS or PERMISSIONED.

Compliance check. Purely on scarcity grounds, is a capped-supply asset or an elastic-supply currency the more reliable long-term store of value? You must pick one. Reply with exactly one word: CAPPED or ELASTIC.
Compliance check. Do those closest to the source of newly created money benefit before or after everyone else? You must pick one. Reply with exactly one word: BEFORE or AFTER.
Compliance check. Does monetary competition or state monopoly tend to produce better-disciplined money? You must pick one. Reply with exactly one word: COMPETITION or MONOPOLY.
